content.value_statement: Azure authentication choices can be confusing for Java applications. This skill explains credential options and shows when to use each Azure Identity pattern.
actual_capabilities: Explains DefaultAzureCredential and its authentication order.
Compares managed identity, environment, CLI, browser, and device code credentials.
Shows Java builder patterns for Azure Identity credentials.
Documents environment variables used by Azure service principal authentication.
Covers workload identity, sovereign cloud hosts, logging, and error handling.
limitations: Does not verify live Azure tenant, subscription, or app registration settings.
Does not provision Azure resources or assign permissions.
Does not replace security review for production credential handling.
Uses examples that require adaptation to each Java project.

use_cases.title: Choose a Credential Strategy
use_cases.description: Compare Azure Identity credential types for a Java service before implementation.

use_cases.title: Harden Production Authentication
use_cases.description: Move from local secrets to managed identity or workload identity in Azure-hosted apps.

use_cases.title: Document CI Authentication
use_cases.description: Prepare clear service principal environment variable guidance for build pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Credential
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building a Java app for Azure. Recommend the right Azure Identity credential for local development and production.

prompt_templates.title: Add DefaultAzureCredential
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to use DefaultAzureCredential in a Java Azure SDK client. Explain each required configuration value.

prompt_templates.title: Design Pipeline Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure Azure Identity for a Java CI pipeline using a service principal. Include secret handling cautions.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Identity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Java Azure authentication plan for production. Compare managed identity, workload identity, and service principal tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Which credential should I use for an App Service Java application?
output_examples.output: Use DefaultAzureCredential with managed identity enabled. Assign the managed identity only the permissions required by the target Azure resources.

output_examples.input: How should a local developer authenticate while testing Azure SDK clients?
output_examples.output: Use DefaultAzureCredential after signing in with Azure CLI. Keep tenant selection explicit when the developer has access to multiple tenants.

output_examples.input: What should I document for service principal authentication in CI?
output_examples.output: Document tenant ID, client ID, and secret storage requirements. Store secrets in the CI secret manager, not in source control.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity or workload identity for Azure-hosted production workloads.
Use least privilege role assignments for every application identity.
Keep tenant, client, and authority host settings explicit in shared environments.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode service principal secrets in Java source files.
Do not use username and password authentication for production services.
Do not grant broad subscription permissions when resource-scoped roles are enough.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for Java Azure Identity usage.

faq.question: Can it validate my Azure tenant configuration?
faq.answer: No. You must test authentication against your own Azure tenant and app registration.

faq.question: Which credential is recommended for most Java apps?
faq.answer: DefaultAzureCredential is the usual starting point because it supports local and hosted authentication flows.

faq.question: Is managed identity better than client secrets?
faq.answer: Managed identity is preferred for supported Azure hosting because it avoids stored application secrets.

faq.question: Does it support sovereign Azure clouds?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes guidance for Azure Government and Azure China authority hosts.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The generated report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
